<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Check current bridge position more carefully
ascii_lines = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')

# Look at the full row 32 and 33

print("Row 33:", ascii_lines[33][10:50])

# Check player position in play area only (rows 12-41)
seg = current_frame.segmentation
for n in seg['nodes']:
    if n['color'] == 'M' and n['pixels'] == 18:
        b = n['boundary']
        rows = [p[0] for p in b]
        cols = [p[1] for p in b]
        print(f"\nPlayer M(18px): rows {min(rows)}-{max(rows)}, cols {min(cols)}-{max(cols)}")

# The bridge needs to reach col 42 (where blocks are)
# Currently bridge ends at col 28
# Each RIGHT adds ~6 cols
# Need ~14 more cols, so ~2-3 more RIGHT presses
# But first let me try 1 RIGHT to see the pattern

result = action(['RIGHT'])
print(f"\nAfter RIGHT: board_changed={last_action_result.get('board_changed')}")

# Check new bridge end
before = last_transition.before_frame.ascii.split('\n')
after = current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
changes = []
for r in range(64):
    for c in range(64):
        if r < len(before) and c < len(before[r]) and r < len(after) and c < len(after[r]):
            if before[r][c] != after[r][c]:
                changes.append((r, c, before[r][c], after[r][c]))
print(f"Cells changed: {len(changes)}")
if changes:
    cols_changed = [c for r,c,_,_ in changes]
    print(f"Col range: {min(cols_changed)}-{max(cols_changed)}")
    
print(f"Row 32 after: {after[32][10:50]}")
print(f"Row 33 after: {after[33][10:50]}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
